topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Define conditional probability P(A|B) as the 're-weighted' probability of A given that B has occurred. Use a Venn Diagram animation where the sample space shrinks from the whole box to just circle B.
sections.example: Visualizing a grid of 100 people: 50 play sports, 20 are athletes. P(Athlete | Sports) focuses only on the 50 sports players.

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
sections.content: Define independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Explain this as 'knowing B tells you nothing new about A'. Visualize this with two separate, non-overlapping probability trees.
sections.example: Flipping a coin twice: The result of the first flip does not change the odds of the second flip being heads.

sections.title: Introduction to Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce the formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Frame this as 'Updating Beliefs'. Use an animation showing a Prior probability evolving into a Posterior probability through the lens of new evidence B.
sections.example: A diagnostic test for a rare disease: P(Disease | Positive Test) is often counter-intuitive because P(Disease) is very low (the Prior).

sections.title: Bayes and Independence: The Critical Link
sections.content: Discuss how independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) = P(A), making the evidence useless. Show a mathematical collapse of the formula to demonstrate why independence is the 'zero-information' state.
sections.example: If a weather report is independent of actual rainfall, the Bayes calculation shows the report provides zero update to the probability of rain.

sections.title: Application: The Detective Case
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge. A detective uses Bayes to update the probability that a suspect is guilty based on a piece of evidence. Contrast the 'Independent' case (evidence is noise) vs. the 'Dependent' case (evidence provides information).
sections.example: A cat-detective (Detective Whiskers) evaluating if a suspect stole the fish: The evidence 'footprint size' is dependent on the suspect's height, allowing for a Bayesian update.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a specific subset.
We shrink our world to circle B.
animations: Create a rectangle representing sample space, with circles A and B. Color #44AAFF.
Highlight circle B with border color #FFCC00.
Animate sample space box fading out, leaving only circle B.
Place a smaller subset 'A intersect B' inside B. Color #FF5555.
Show P(A|B) as the ratio of area(A intersect B) to area(B).

storyboard.title: The Concept of Independence
lecture_lines: Independent events do not influence each other.
Knowing B tells you nothing about A.
Probabilities remain unchanged by new information.
animations: Display two separate probability tree diagrams on screen. Color #00FF00.
Label top branch P(A), bottom branch P(not A). Color #FFFFFF.
Animate both trees branching independently with same probabilities. Highlight labels.

storyboard.title: Introduction to Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem lets us update our beliefs.
We combine a prior with new evidence.
This gives us a refined posterior probability.
It is essential for diagnostic testing.
Evidence shifts the probability weight effectively.
animations: Display formula P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B) in center. Color #FFFFFF.
Represent Prior P(A) as a bar chart. Color #888888.
Introduce Evidence B as a light pulse moving toward Prior bar. Color #FFCC00.
Animate Prior bar changing size to Posterior P(A|B). Color #FF5555.
Add a summary label 'Updated Belief'. Color #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Bayes and Independence: The Critical Link
lecture_lines: The formula collapses when events are independent.
animations: Display Bayes formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Color #FFFFFF.
Flash P(A|B) = P(A) to show independence. Color #FF5555.
Animate the Bayes formula fading out while 'Independence' text appears. Color #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Application: The Detective Case
lecture_lines: Detectives use Bayes to solve cases.
animations: Display a silhouette of a detective. Color #44AAFF.
Place evidence icons (footprints) around the detective. Color #FFCC00.
Show the probability bar increasing as evidence is added. Color #FF5555.
